item.title: Hunters kill kidnappers who came for ₦10m ransom in Kano
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Two suspected bandits have been killed by local hunters, while ₦10 million paid as ransom for a kidnapped man has been recovered in Falgore Forest, Doguwa Local Government Area of Kano State. This was contained in a statement by CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, Police Public Relations Officer on Saturday. According to the statement, the kidnapped victim, identified as 45-year-old Kabiru Aliyu of Falgore Village, was released unharmed after the suspects collected the ransom “The incident occurred at about midnight on Saturday, when three suspected bandits allegedly emerged from Falgore Forest to collect the money demanded for Aliyu’s release. According to the statement, the victim was kidnapped on September 11, 2026, and had spent several days in captivity before his release. The police said that shortly after collecting the ₦10 million ransom and releasing the victim, the suspects were ambushed by local hunters known as Yan Bula while returning to their hideout in Falgore Forest. “During the ambush, two of the suspected bandits were neutralised, while the third suspect escaped with injuries. The entire ransom sum of ₦10 million was recovered intact from the neutralised suspects,” the statement said. The command said preliminary investigations had identified one of the suspects killed as Dogo Isah, a commercial motorcycle rider from Maigwanda Village in Kubau Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The police said the suspects were believed to have come from Maigwanda Village before the incident. The Commissioner of Police in Kano State, CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the Yan Bula hunters for their efforts in supporting security operations in the area. Bakori said the hunters’ activities continued to complement the police operation against kidnapping, banditry and other violent crimes in the state under Operation Kukan Kura. Following the incident, the commissioner directed the Area Commander, Divisional Police Officers and tactical teams operating in the area to immediately search the forest and surrounding communities for the fleeing suspect. He also directed the teams to intensify efforts to arrest the suspect and recover any weapons used by the group. The police further disclosed that the rescued victim had been debriefed, medically examined and reunited with his family. The command assured residents of its commitment to protecting lives and property. Vanguard News The post Hunters kill kidnappers who came for ₦10m ransom in Kano appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sahel states restart dialogue with ECOWAS
item.description: Three junta-ruled Sahel states on Saturday resumed dialogue with the ECOWAS regional bloc which they quit over 18 months ago, agreeing to work together towards a cooperation “framework agreement”. Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso, led by juntas that came to power between 2020 and 2023, left the Economic Community of West African States in January 2025, after teaming up to create their own group, the Alliance of Sahel States (AES). Talks between ECOWAS and the AES had been under way since January 2025 but Saturday was their first official ministerial meeting. In a joint statement issued Saturday evening, the two sides “welcomed the spirit of fraternity, mutual respect and openness” of the talks, and stressed the importance of maintaining relations of “good neighbourliness” particularly with “respect for sovereignty”. They agreed to “set up joint thematic working groups (…) to reach a framework cooperation agreement”. The AES delegation was led by Karamoko Jean-Marie Traore, Burkina Faso’s foreign minister, and the Ecowas delegation by Cheikh Niang, his Senegalese counterpart. The AES juntas have all turned their backs on France, the former colonial power, and by extension on several countries in the region such as Cete d’Ivoire and Benin, which they consider too close to Paris. The trio have moved closer politically to Moscow, claiming an anti-imperialist and pro-sovereignty vision, and they have bitterly criticised west African coastal countries which have remained close to France. item.title: Dubois destroys Wardley in round two to retain WBO heavyweight crown
item.description: Daniel Dubois scored a crushing second-round knockout victory over fellow Briton Fabio Wardley to retain his World Boxing Organization heavyweight crown on Saturday. In a much-anticipated rematch of their bruising 11-round classic earlier this year, Dubois dominated Wardley from the opening bell to batter his rival into submission in the second round. Dubois dropped Wardley after 17 seconds of the contest at the O2 Arena in London, catching the challenger flush on the chin with a huge overhand right. The 29-year-old Dubois continued to land punches at will throughout the first round, which finished with Wardley clinging on desperately under a barrage a punches on the ropes. The second round started as the first had ended, with the 6ft 5in Dubois uncorking an array of punches that left Wardley in desperate trouble. With Dubois unloading on a defenceless Wardley, the towel came in after two minutes and 21 seconds of the round. Dubois improved to 24-3-0 with 23 knockouts while the 31-year-old Wardley fell to 20-2-1. item.title: Ambassador Dele Cole devoted his life to national service — Tinubu
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has expressed sadness over the death of the veteran journalist and diplomat, Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, saying that the late statesman devoted his life to national service. Ambassador Cole died at the age of 86. President Tinubu, in his tribute titled “Farewell to Ambassador Dele Cole, distinguished diplomat, journalist and public servant,” said the late veteran journalist brought distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics. The tribute read: “I received with profound sadness the news of the passing of Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, a distinguished diplomat, journalist, politician, and public servant, who died at 86. “Ambassador Cole devoted his life to national service, bringing distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics. “His career reflected the enduring value of dialogue, tact, mutual respect and the pursuit of shared interests in advancing national development and international cooperation. “His contributions to Nigeria’s media landscape were particularly notable. As Managing Director of the Daily Times, he upheld the vital role of the press in holding public officials accountable, speaking truth to power, and strengthening democratic governance. His legacy in journalism and public life remains an enduring part of our national story. “At 86, Ambassador Dele Cole witnessed defining moments in Nigeria’s history and contributed to the nation’s development through his work in the media, diplomacy and public service. His life stands as a testament to the value of experience, principled engagement and commitment to the public good. “As we mourn his passing, I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, professional associates and all whose lives he touched. I pray that memories of his remarkable life will bring them comfort and strength at this difficult time. “May Almighty God grant Ambassador Cole eternal rest and give his family and all who mourn him the fortitude to bear this profound loss.” The post Ambassador Dele Cole devoted his life to national service — Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 19 Dead, 25 Hurt In Stampede At India Religious Gathering
item.description: At least 19 people were killed and two dozen more injured Saturday in eastern India after a stampede that occurred during sudden rainfall at a Hindu religious gathering, officials and Indian media said. West Bengal’s Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari told reporters the fatalities included a seven-year-old girl, adding that 25 other people were injured outside a pavilion “in a stampede” at the Hindu festival of Durga Puja in the city of Kolkata. “Six bodies have so far been identified,” Adhikari said. A senior police official at the scene told AFP an announcement caused “commotion” after it started raining at night and the “crowd waiting outside the pandal (pavilion) was pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.” Afterwards, medics were seen moving injured people on stretchers, including a police officer, into a local hospital. Several relatives of victims cried and held one another as they mourned the loss of loved ones. Medical workers move an injured police officer on a stretcher, following the Durga Puja Pandal stampede, in front of the emergency building of Calcutta Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata on October 16, 2026. Photo by STRINGER / AFP Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the tragedy in a short statement on Facebook. “The stampede in Kolkata is saddening. Condolences to the bereaved families. Wishing the injured a speedy recovery,” he wrote. “The West Bengal Government is providing all possible help to the affected families.” Adhikari originally announced 17 fatalities. The Press Trust of India (PTI) reported the death toll rose by two to 19, quoting Adhikari in a later statement. Nine dead bodies have been released to their families, the PTI reported. It also said police have taken the closed circuit footage of the festival and authorities would initiate action against those seen on CCTV who appeared to fail in their responsibility for crowd control. Videos shot before the stampede appeared to show large crowds of people waiting to enter the pavilion, in an area with narrow lanes that allow only a few people to walk in at a time, according to Indian Express. Deadly crowd incidents are a frequent occurrence at Indian mass events, such as religious festivals, due to poor management and safety lapses. Last year, a stampede at India’s Kumbh Mela religious fair killed 30 people and injured several others, and 11 fans were crushed to death in Bengaluru during celebrations for the local cricket team’s first Indian Premier League title. The same year, 36 people were killed after a stampede broke out at a campaign rally of a popular actor-turned-politician in southern Tamil Nadu state. In 2024, 121 people were killed in northern Uttar Pradesh state during a Hindu religious gathering. item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Nigeria’s full economic recovery depends entirely on sustaining the bold reform policies initiated by President Bola Tinubu. Wike said this on Saturday, at the Rainbow Coalition’s stakeholders’ consultation in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area of Rivers. He said that only the continuation of the current administration’s economic direction could permanently pull the country back from the brink of collapse. He noted that the hard economic choices being implemented presently were necessary remedies to salvage a system that was virtually “dead” when Tinubu took office. “Only the continuation of the economic reforms initiated by the Tinubu government can bring this country back from the economic comatose it was in before this present administration took over,” he said. He said that the presidential candidate of the Africa Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Abubakar Atiku and his vice, Rotimi Amaechi, had nothing to offer to Nigerians. The minister urged residents of the state not to surrender the country’s progress to “career politicians” and “political opportunists” whom he likened to “chronic pool betters” who repeatedly gamble with public trust. According to him, supporting politicians who have made decades-long pursuits for power would mean diverting national funds to recoup lost campaign expenses rather than consolidating economic gains. item.title: FG Warns Return Of Fuel Subsidy Can Trigger Capital Flight
item.description: The Federal Government has warned that a return to the fuel subsidy can trigger capital flight, put pressure on the naira, and undermine the gains of its economic reforms. The warning came at a media briefing in Bangkok, Thailand, at the conclusion of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings. The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele; the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, Olayemi Cardoso; and the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Atiku Bagudu, addressed Nigeria’s economic outlook following the conclusion of the meeting. Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy Taiwo Oyedele said on October 8, 2026, that FG’s 30-day fuel reduction is not a return of the subsidy. The finance minister said investors have repeatedly sought assurances that the government will not reverse the removal of fuel subsidy or the unification of exchange rates, particularly as the country approaches another election cycle. Oyedele argued that any signal of a possible return to subsidies could prompt investors to withdraw their capital, putting pressure on the foreign exchange market and the naira. The Minister of Finance and the Central Bank Governor arrive for the final briefing by the Nigerian delegation to the 2026 IMF-World Bank Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. After five days of deliberations, the delegation highlighted some of the key takeaways from the event, especially as they impact the administration’s economic policies. ﻿ It clarified the decision to discount the retail price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS). The delegation also announced the Federal Government’s seven per cent economic growth target. In his remarks, the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning emphasised the need for fiscal and monetary authorities to work together to sustain the gains of the reforms. Debt, climate, AI, and inequality topped the agenda at the World Bank-IMF meeting attended by Nigeria and 190 other countries in Thailand. At the meeting, Nigeria called for comprehensive reforms of the IMF and the World Bank to give developing economies a strong voice in global financial decisions, improve access to financing and strengthen their capacity to withstand economic shocks. While presenting the Group of Twenty-Four (G-24) 2026 annual meeting communiqué in Bangkok, Thailand, on the sidelines of the World Bank/IMF Annual Meetings, Oyedele said geopolitical conflicts, trade uncertainties, volatile commodity prices and climate shocks are threatening global economic growth. According to him, the challenges disproportionately affect emerging markets and developing economies, undermining efforts to create jobs and achieve inclusive transformation. item.title: Hunters kill two suspected bandits, recover ₦10m ransom in Kano
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Two suspected bandits have been killed by local hunters, while ₦10 million paid as ransom for a kidnapped man has been recovered in Falgore Forest, Doguwa Local Government Area of Kano State. This was contained in a statement signed by CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, Police Public Relations Officer, on Saturday. According to the statement, the kidnapped victim, identified as 45-year-old Kabiru Aliyu of Falgore Village, was released unharmed after the suspects collected the ransom The incident occurred at about midnight on Saturday, when three suspected bandits allegedly emerged from Falgore Forest to collect the money demanded for Aliyu’s release. According to the statement, the victim was kidnapped on September 11, 2026, and had spent several days in captivity before his release. The police said that shortly after collecting the ₦10 million ransom and releasing the victim, the suspects were ambushed by local hunters known as Yan Bula while returning to their hideout in Falgore Forest. “During the ambush, two of the suspected bandits were neutralised, while the third suspect escaped with injuries. The entire ransom sum of ₦10 million was recovered intact from the neutralised suspects,” the statement said. The command said preliminary investigations had identified one of the suspects killed as Dogo Isah, a commercial motorcycle rider from Maigwanda Village in Kubau Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The police said the suspects were believed to have come from Maigwanda Village before the incident. The Commissioner of Police in Kano State, CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the Yan Bula hunters for their efforts in supporting security operations in the area. Bakori said the hunters’ activities continued to complement the police operation against kidnapping, banditry and other violent crimes in the state under Operation Kukan Kura. Following the incident, the commissioner directed the Area Commander, Divisional Police Officers and tactical teams operating in the area to immediately search the forest and surrounding communities for the fleeing suspect. He also directed the teams to intensify efforts to arrest the suspect and recover any weapons used by the group. The police further disclosed that the rescued victim had been debriefed, medically examined and reunited with his family. The command assured residents of its commitment to protecting lives and property. The post Hunters kill two suspected bandits, recover ₦10m ransom in Kano appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Benue 2027: Ex-Otukpo council chair, APC, ADC, ZLP chieftains defect to PDP
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A former Caretaker Chairman of Otukpo Local Government Area of Benue state, Mr. Inalegwu Adakonye, has defected from the All Progressives Congress (APC) to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), alongside other political stakeholders and their supporters from the APC, African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Zenith Labour Party (ZLP). The defection featured several prominent political figures from Adoka and Ugboju communities in Otukpo council. Among prominent politicians who weekend in Otukpo joined the PDP with the former chairman of Otukpo were Adoga Edache, popularly known as Ebo, from the ADC; Emmanuel Akoche of the ZLP; Garuba Sule of the APC; and Mr. John Ojonye, ADC Chairman of Ugboju Ehaji Ward, alongside other party members and supporters. Explaining his decision to return to the PDP, Adakonye said the party’s ideology of inclusiveness and collective participation informed his choice, arguing that its approach to politics differed from that of the APC. He said “the PDP treats its members as one family and offer a platform where everyone can participate. And I am confident that the party is best positioned to rescue Benue state from bad governance.” Adakonye, who led APC members from Adoka and Ugboju into the PDP, also cited the emergence of Dr. Oyije Ogbenjuwa as the party’s deputy governorship candidate as a factor behind their decision. He said they could not afford to remain outside the political movement of their brother and friend, who he expressed confidence would soon become the deputy governor of the state. The defectors also cited the PDP’s people-oriented ideology, leadership and prospects in forthcoming elections as reasons for abandoning their former parties for the opposition platform. Receiving the new members were the PDP deputy governorship candidate, Dr. Ogbenjuwa; the Otukpo Local Government PDP Chairman, Godwin Ochapa; the party’s House of Assembly candidate for Otukpo/Akpa, Johnson Egli; its candidate for Adoka/Ugboju, Gabriel Olofu; and the Senior Legislative Aide to the Senate President, Chief George Alli. Speaking on behalf of the party, Ogbenjuwa welcomed the defectors and assured them of “equal opportunities and full integration into the party’s activities.” He described their decision to join the PDP “as evidence of the party’s growing acceptability across Benue South Senatorial District, and your support will further strengthen our political base ahead of future elections.” The new members, in turn, pledged their loyalty and commitment to working for the success of the PDP at all levels. My apology to the parents of the deceased and to the people and government of Niger State,” he told the commission. ‎ ‎The former state commandant expressed regret that the incident occurred during his tenure, acknowledging that the deaths could have been avoided. ‎ ‎He told the commission that he assumed duty as Niger State NSCDC Commandant on August 25, 2025, and remained in office until September 18, 2026. ‎ ‎According to him, the operation at a mining site along the M. I. Wushishi Housing Estate in Minna followed written and oral complaints from residents who alleged that mining activities were disrupting their community. ‎ ‎Aniviye said he visited the site on September 15, 2026, and subsequently directed the command’s Head of Operations, Assistant Commandant of Corps Joha Achagwa, to act on the complaints. ‎ ‎He explained that the Mining Marshal Unit was deployed, leading to the arrest of suspected illegal miners during an operation on the evening of September 16. ‎ ‎The following day, however, several detainees were reported dead in the corps’ custody. ‎ ‎Aniviye told the commission that he received a telephone call informing him that some suspects had died in detention, prompting him to rush to the command headquarters, where he found several bodies lying on the floor of the cell. ‎ ‎He said he contacted Niger State Governor, Umaru Bago, who directed that the bodies be taken to a hospital. Aniviye added that he also informed the Commissioner of Police and the Director of the Department of State Services about the incident. ‎ ‎The suspended commandant further disclosed that arrangements had been made to arraign the suspects in court on September 17 before the deaths occurred. ‎ ‎However, testimony by the suspended head of the NSCDC legal unit, Assistant Commandant of Corps Stephen Tsado, raised further questions about the treatment of the detainees and the handling of minors arrested during the operation. ‎ ‎Tsado, whose responsibilities included preparing case files, forwarding cases for prosecution and advising the commandant on legal matters, said he noticed that some of the arrested suspects were minors and advised Aniviye to release them to their parents on bail. ‎ ‎He told the commission that he personally urged the commandant to act on his advice to protect the rights of the minors but could not explain why the recommendation was not implemented. ‎ ‎“I advised him to grant them bail to their parents,” Tsado said. ‎ ‎The commission also heard testimony from Nurse Maryam Etang of the NSCDC medical unit, who said she visited the detention cell as part of her routine duties on September 16 and 17. ‎ ‎Etang disclosed that one of the suspects was coughing seriously on September 17, around the time the bodies were being removed from the cell. ‎ ‎She also said she was shocked to discover the body of one Emeka Emmanuel among those removed, insisting that he was not among the miners arrested during the operation. ‎ ‎Her testimony raised further questions about Emmanuel’s presence in the cell and the circumstances that led to his death. ‎ ‎The commission is expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths, examine the treatment of the detainees and determine whether there were lapses in the conduct of the operation and the subsequent handling of those in custody. ‎ ‎In earlier proceedings, a mortician at the Minna General Hospital told the commission that 33 bodies were delivered to the hospital’s mortuary, a figure that differs from the 37 deaths reported by the Niger State Government and other authorities. Governor Umaru Bago in September inaugurated a nine-member judicial commission of inquiry to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths of 37 miners in the custody of the NSCDC in the state. The deaths of the miners triggered a protest in the state, prompting Governor Bago to declare a 24-hour curfew in Minna, the state capital. Following the tragedy, President Bola Tinubu ordered a full and transparent investigation, saying that the government would not tolerate mass deaths arising from official negligence, dereliction of duty, or failure by public officials to protect the lives placed under their care. Similarly, the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, announced the suspension of 20 NSCDC officers in connection with the deaths. item.title: How my mother was kidnapped over $2.4bn subsidy fraud — Okonjo-Iweala
item.description: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, the Director-General of the World Trade Organisation, WTO, has recalled how her investigation into an alleged $2.4bn fuel subsidy fraud in Nigeria led her mother’s kidnapping. Read Also: Okonjo-Iweala’s mother, 82, kidnapped Okonjo-Iweala narrated her experience in an interview with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua. She said the kidnappers’ demands were that she resigns as the Minister of Finance and leave the country. On how the ordeal began, she said her office noticed a sharp increase in subsidy claims, so she began to probe. Her words: “So I went to the president and said, look, something is going on here. Could we audit the accounts? And he said, yes, go ahead. “And we found about $2.4 billion worth of fraud. So we refused to pay.” That was when they took her mother. Okonjo-Iweala said the five-day ordeal was among the most painful periods of her life. “I was told (by the kidnappers) that for her to be released, I should resign and leave the country. “She was held in the middle of a forest, and one night she escaped. She’s still alive. She’s 96 now.” “It was a terrible, terrible five-day ordeal. I think the worst in my life,” she said. Okonjo-Iweala said initially she felt paralysed by fear and considered resigning. She added that that the experience left her with a sense of guilt that she still carries. “I never dreamt my parents could ever be touched in this way, that people would be that evil,” she said. On her father’s reaction at the time, she said: “He said, ‘We don’t give in to blackmail’. And he said, ‘You’ve got to carry on. You’ve got to go to work’.” Okonjo-Iweala served as Minister of Finance under President Goodluck Jonathan. Her mother, Kamene Okonjo, was kidnapped from her home in Ogwashi-Uku, Delta State, in December 2012. Read the kidnap story HERE . item.title: To suggest Anthony Kila hasn’t gone to school is stupid — Utomi
item.description: Political Economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, says he cannot guarantee that embattled professor Anthony Kila has never made mistakes but to suggest that he has never gone to school is spectacularly unfair to his personality. Utomi made this known on his verified Facebook page in Lagos on Saturday, saying that Kila is a good man. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) recalls that Kila is currently at the centre of a major scandal regarding his academic credentials. In October, an investigative report published by Premium Times revealed that Kila allegedly falsified all of his higher education qualifications, including his bachelor’s, master’s, doctorate (PhD) degrees, and his rank as a professor. Utomi, reacting to the online claim, said that there was no evidence to support the claim that Anthony Kila (popularly known as “Prof Kila”) had never gone to school. “I know Anthony Kila. I became aware of all the trending discussions about his career rather late. “I have never had any reason to ask about his certificates or letters of appointment, so I cannot claim to have those details. “However, if he has never gone to school, then those who have must ask for a refund. “We watched the cyber mob bully Jason Arday, the youngest Black professor ever appointed at Cambridge, to his early death. “Incidentally, I first met Anthony Kila in the city of Cambridge, England, in 2006, when I was beginning a run for the office of President of Nigeria.” Utomi said that among those in the mob that sought to lynch Arday were white professors, who had been pardoned for mistakes of a far worse nature. He said he did not know who might be going after Kila in a country where many people confer academic and non-academic titles on themselves, while the media, through its status-conferring function, elevates them to celebrity status. He, however, said that this does not seem normal, saying he could empathise because he has had a similar experience. Utomi said: “Years ago, when a journalist tried to suggest that my stay at Volkswagen Nigeria had something to do with its demise, I offered ₦12 million to anyone who could produce a shred of evidence to support that claim. Fifteen years on, no one has come forward to claim the bounty. “When I became the first professor of Pan-African (Pan-Atlantic) parent of the Lagos Business School, someone at UNILAG went, “…huh, until he found out that the evaluating team was led by the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan.” “If professors like Adele Jinadu in Political Science and Joe Umo at UNILAG had not met me in graduate school abroad and interacted with my Head of Department, Elinor Lin Ostrom, who went on to become the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Economics, someone may have written something demeaning about my education. “Kila is a smart and good man. I cannot guarantee he has not made mistakes but to suggest he has not gone to school is spectacularly stupid.” (NAN) The post To suggest Anthony Kila hasn’t gone to school is stupid —

item.title: Unstoppable Barca thrash Betis to extend perfect start
item.description: Hansi Flick’s dominant Barcelona routed 10-man Real Betis 5-2 on Saturday to return five points clear at the top of La Liga. Teenage winger Lamine Yamal scored a brilliant goal for the Spanish champions, with Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric Garcia and Dani Olmo also finding the net at La Cartuja stadium in Seville. Betis, third, had Facundo Bernal sent off for a headbutt on Yamal early in the second half of a pulsating clash. Barca set a new club record for victories at the start of a league campaign and equalled the all-time record of nine, set by Real Madrid in the 1968/69 season. Flick’s side boast 11 wins from 11 games across all competitions. “Once again the team has shown its attacking potential, but it’s also true we’re giving quite a bit away, and that’s probably where the improvement has to come from too,” Rodri told DAZN. Earlier Atletico, second, snatched a late 1-0 win at Espanyol and are five points behind Barca, while Betis are eight points adrift of the leaders and Real Madrid, fourth, host Sevilla on Sunday. Betis rested several players, including key midfielder Isco, ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Feyenoord. Manuel Pellegrini’s side still gave Barca a stern test, after the Catalan giants went ahead through a sensational Yamal strike in the 10th minute. The 19-year-old turned sharply on the edge of the box to escape Bernal and then exquisitely curled into the top corner. “(It was) an incredible goal, we’ve got used to him doing this lately, I have to say,” added Rodri. “In the end, players like that make the difference. But I try to focus on the other things he brings… (like) hard work, a lot of solidarity with the team, understanding the game and where he could find space.” – Defensive flaws – Despite their irresistible attacking play, Barca’s clear weakness under Flick has been their defence and Betis were level before the half-hour mark. A corner came all the way through the box and was recycled by Pablo Fornals, who crossed for Valentin Gomez to head home, getting in front of Barca defender Xavi Espart. Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri put Barca back in front with a header from a corner, before Giovani Lo Celso thought he had equalised in spectacular fashion for the hosts. However the Argentine midfielder’s long-range goal was ruled out for a handball by Cucho Hernandez earlier in the move, much to Betis’ chagrin. Jesus extended Barca’s lead six minutes into the second half from Yamal’s cut-back, moments after having another goal ruled out for offside. Ez Abde immediately pulled one back for Betis during a wild spell, and in the aftermath they were reduced to 10 men when Bernal was sent off for a headbutt on Yamal, who was booked for his part in a confrontation between several players from both sides. Barca added their fourth when Pau Cubarsi nodded the ball across to Garcia to pounce from close range. It was the eighth time this season Flick’s free-scoring side have scored four goals or more in a match.

item.title: Diaz dazzles as Bayern batter Leipzig to go top

Diaz had faced criticism after four league games without a goal but the Colombian sparked to life to terrorise Leipzig defender Lukas Klostermann down the left. item.title: ‘I can’t die like this’: flydubai pilot recounts ordeal of cockpit attack
item.description: The captain of a flydubai flight whose co-pilot attacked him with an axe in an alleged bid to bring down the plane said one thought kept running through his head as the harrowing ordeal unfolded: “You can’t die like this.” Read Also: ‘I could not let all those people die’ — Indian pilot recounts flydubai ordeal Indian pilot Smit Machchhar recounted the “traumatic” experience to Sky News Arabia in his first interview since the incident late last month in which he, passengers and other crew members were credited with averting disaster on the Tel Aviv-bound flight. With his head and one hand bandaged and glasses perched on his nose, Machchhar spoke from his hospital bed in the UAE. “My vision was restricted to a few inches,” said the pilot, describing the effect of being struck in the back of the head with an emergency axe by his co-pilot, who had positioned himself behind Machchhar’s seat. At first thinking that a part of the airplane’s ceiling had come loose, he then received several more blows and was wounded in the hand as he tried to shield himself. Machchhar recalled struggling to open the cockpit door so another pilot who was travelling on board could get inside. “So I was screaming his name and I was trying, because the switch that was very close to me to open the door, I was trying to just get help in,” he said. “But I remember being able to open the door,” he went on, only for it to shut again. “And at that point, I felt all the blood, you know, everything rushing down, my energy, everything, I was just, I was barely staying in consciousness.” “Soon after that, that was the time when I heard the engine sounds going down. And then immediately after that I felt the aircraft going into a dive.” According to findings released by the Emirati attorney general, Machchhar’s 29-year-old Omani co-pilot had planned to use the plane to carry out a suicide attack on the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, inspired by the September 11, 2001 attacks in New York. He claimed to have acted alone, something investigators are still working to verify. The prosecutor found that the other pilot on board, having seen the cockpit door open and close “in an unusual manner”, entered the flight deck and with the help of another crew member and passengers, subdued the co-pilot and regained control of the aircraft. The jet, which plunged violently during the fray, was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Machchhar said the way his colleague was able to intervene and safely land the plane was “commendable”. “It’s something that I’ll keep with me till I die.” The post ‘I can’t die like this’: flydubai pilot recounts ordeal of cockpit attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gunmen kill two policemen, set station, operation van ablaze in Abia
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe Unknown gunmen have killed two policemen and burnt buildings and a patrol van at the Uratta Police Division, in Aba, Abia State. Confirming the incident, Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the Command, DSP Maureen Chinaka, disclosed that the hoodlums attacked the division with explosives, resulting in a fire that damaged part of the building and the divisional patrol van. She added that two police officers lost their lives, while three inspectors sustained injuries and are currently receiving medical attention. The Command further clarified that no firearms or ammunition were carted away by the attackers during the incident. The PPRO explained that the Commissioner of Police, Abia State Command, CP Wilfred Afolabi, had personally led an operational team to the area. She also stated that the team combed the surrounding environment and restored calm, while intensified security operations and monitoring are ongoing to apprehend the hoodlums. The PPRO assured that the Command will deploy all necessary operational and intelligence resources to identify and apprehend those responsible, assuring that the hoodlums will be brought to justice. “The Command extends its heartfelt condolences to the families of the fallen officers and the entire Police family over this painful loss. “Residents are urged to remain calm, vigilant and to support the Police with credible information that could assist the ongoing investigation. “Information can be reported at the nearest police station, through the suggestion boxes and contact details of the DPO’s provided at police divisions, or via the Command’s emergency hotlines: 08035415405,08079210004, 08079210005, 08079210006.” Vanguard gathered that Governor Alex Otti had visited the police station as well as the injured policemen at the hospital. item.description: Israeli settlers on Saturday attacked a convoy of European diplomats and beat up a visiting French mayor, in a new escalation of violence during the Palestinian olive harvest, witnesses and diplomats told AFP. The 78-year-old mayor said masked settlers yelled defamatory comments about France, kicked him and hit him with iron bars as he joined Palestinian olive farmers in the West Bank alongside the top French and Belgian representatives in Jerusalem and Polish diplomats. “I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government,” Bernard Baudoux, mayor of the northern French town of Aulnoye-Aymeries, told AFP after he was attacked. “The whole world needs to know what’s happening,” he said. “For me, I’ll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here.” Baudoux, who was wearing a sash with the French tricolour, was seen collapsed on the side of the car after the attack but he did not need hospital care. The attack came just one day after settlers beat an American photographer for The Washington Post, who was in moderate condition with broken vertebrae on Saturday.
